title: All-In Site Quotes for Chassis-Free Homes
one_liner: Type a parcel address, get a fixed-price foundation, utility-hookup and permit package for a factory-built home, delivered by a local crew network.
customer: Manufactured and modular home dealers, small landowners and buyers, and factory builders that need site-work partners. Rural and small-town jurisdictions benefit indirectly.
problem: The ROAD to Housing Act (signed July 11, 2026) kills the steel-chassis rule, worth about $10K or 10% of unit cost, though HUD must still publish standards. Cheaper units will ship, but the sale is decided by unknown site costs: foundation, utilities, septic or well, set crew and permits. These stay local and human, and dealers cannot quote the all-in price.
solution: A parcel-level site-cost estimator using soils, flood zone, utility distance, jurisdiction fees and foundation type, returning a fixed-price quote in 24 hours. It is backed by a vetted crew network (excavation, foundation, set, utilities) on 7-day pay, one accountable contract, and packaged construction-to-perm financing. Begin with conventional manufactured homes on permanent foundations, so revenue starts before HUD standards land.
why_now: ROAD Act enacted July 2026 with HUD standards pending and a federal showcase of factory-built homes. Site work is exactly where the labor shortage and permit friction bite hardest. Standard duplex and townhome blueprints are being funded.
revenue_model: 10-15% GC margin on site packages ($30-60K). $300-500 quote fee credited on booking. Dealer referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone watching the ROAD Act watches factories and financing. The bottleneck will be the last 100 feet, and price uncertainty there kills the cheap-home pitch. The first team that gives a real all-in number becomes the dealers' default site partner and captures the margin the factory cannot.
first_30_days: Choose a county cluster in Texas or the Southeast where manufactured homes are common. Sign two dealers. Build the estimator from public GIS, flood and utility data. Deliver 20 free quotes and convert 2-3 to jobs with existing subs.

title: Get Paid to Care: Family Caregiver Enrollment
one_liner: A navigator that gets family caregivers onto Medicaid and VA payrolls, then becomes the fiscal intermediary that pays them.
customer: Adult children and spouses (45-70) giving 20+ hours a week of unpaid care to a low-income parent or veteran. Secondary buyers are Area Agencies on Aging, Medicaid managed-care plans and state Medicaid agencies that pay fiscal-intermediary fees.
problem: 59M family caregivers gave 49.5B unpaid hours in 2024 (about $1T) and lose roughly $21k a year in income. Every state has Medicaid self-direction, many pay relatives, and the VA has Veteran-Directed Care. But the rules differ by state, the assessment sets the hours, and agencies and fiscal intermediaries earn more by placing an outside aide.
solution: Phase 1 is a state-by-state 'can I get paid?' screener plus done-with-you enrollment: eligibility, application packet, coaching for the nurse assessment (which sets hours), employee onboarding, timesheet and electronic-visit-verification coaching, and appeals. Phase 2 is to become a licensed fiscal intermediary (payroll, background checks, EVV) in states that allow several vendors, and to bill the state a monthly per-participant fee.
why_now: About $911B in federal Medicaid cuts plus work requirements, 41 states with HCBS waitlists over 600k people (average wait 15 months), and Wisconsin agencies 'not able to take new clients' after the 2026 visa and TPS shocks. States now have to lean on the caregiver already in the house.
revenue_model: Families pay a flat $349-499 per successful enrollment, or a lower fee plus a first-year success fee. Phase 2 adds state or MCO fiscal-intermediary per-member-per-month fees. AAAs can pay for referral-sourced enrollment.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is partly a payment-eligibility problem, not a bodies problem. The gatekeepers who could help families avoid agencies are the agencies and legacy fiscal intermediaries, so no one with a business incentive teaches families the paid-relative pathway.
first_30_days: Pick two states where relatives can be paid and enrollment is open (California's IHSS is the obvious one). Publish the screener and state guides, then capture leads through caregiver support groups, Facebook groups and elder-law firms. Sell a $349 concierge enrollment to the first 20 families and measure approval rate and approved hours.

title: Scam-Compound Geo-Intelligence for Compliance Teams
one_liner: A monthly geospatial register of scam compounds, built from satellite imagery and RF data, that lets exchanges and banks flag payees and merchants with a physical nexus to them.
customer: Financial-crime investigators and sanctions teams at crypto exchanges, stablecoin off-ramps, OTC desks, Asian correspondent banks and payment processors. Secondary: anti-scam consortia (for example GASA members) and the US/UK scam-center task forces that agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate takedowns.
problem: Chainalysis puts 2025 scam revenue near $17B, with AI-enabled operations averaging $3.2M versus $719K, and US investment fraud alone hit $8.65B. On-chain tools label wallets but nobody maps the physical compounds (Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos, now spreading) to counterparties. Compounds relocate after raids, and enforcement and sanctions need evidence of place, not just of transactions.
solution: A register of suspected compounds and displacement corridors built from optical and SAR change detection (perimeter walls, dormitory blocks, razor-wire, rooftop dish counts, nighttime lights) plus purchased RF-geolocation data on satellite-terminal uplinks, cross-referenced to corporate registries and Telegram guarantee marketplaces. Delivered as a risk API and CSV: 'this payee's declared address, IP cluster or KYC address is within X km of a flagged compound', with analyst-reviewed confidence tiers and evidence packets for suspicious-activity reports. Also a relocation forecast near border economic zones.
why_now: The US and UK agreed on 4 Sept 2026 to coordinate scam-center takedowns, and 2025 sanctions on the Prince Group showed enforcement appetite. Commercial revisit rates and cheap SAR now make monthly monitoring affordable. Reporting has documented satellite-internet terminals at compounds, giving them an RF and imagery signature.
revenue_model: $3-8K per compound-exposure assessment for investigations teams and $10-25K per month for the risk feed and API. Consortium data-sharing licences later.
non_obvious_insight: On-chain analytics see money but not place, and compounds are physically huge, slow to build and hard to hide, unlike wallets. They sit in a gap between defense-intel EO buyers and commercial AML, so no one serves them. Compliance teams need geographic-nexus evidence to justify de-risking specific corridors instead of blanket bans, and a place-based register gives regulators something to point to.
first_30_days: Validate signatures on known compounds (KK Park, Shwe Kokko, Sihanoukville, Golden Triangle zone) with Sentinel-1 and 2 plus $5-10K of commercial imagery credit. Publish a free 'Compound Atlas' of 30 sites with human-reviewed confidence tiers. Pitch 5 exchange investigations heads and one anti-scam NGO consortium, and sell 2-3 paid assessments.

title: Asset-Light Black Mass Desk Under BIS Rule
one_liner: A trading and compliance desk that becomes the default outlet for US black mass sellers, using the rule's toll-processing exception instead of building plants.
customer: Scrap managers at US cell gigafactories and black-mass aggregators (sellers), who pay brokerage and compliance fees. Toll processors with idle hydromet capacity pay for feed access.
problem: Since the Aug 27, 2026 BIS/DPA rule, sellers must allocate 100% of monthly black mass sales to US buyers. Domestic buyers are thin after Ascend's Chapter 11 and Li-Cycle's bankruptcy, and DOE grants were cancelled. Sellers face legal exposure, a one-sided bid, and assay disputes. BIS has said more materials may be added.
solution: A desk that (1) certifies sampling and assay per lot, (2) documents and allocates monthly volumes across US buyers, (3) structures toll-processing corridors. These run through domestic hydromet capacity, or through foreign processors whose intermediates return to the US, which the rule exempts. (4) It issues a per-lot compliance file. It never owns a plant, only feedstock relationships and the legal wrapper.
why_now: The BIS temporary final rule (Aug 2026) makes domestic allocation mandatory and toll-processing the only export route. Manufacturing scrap is about two-thirds of North American battery feedstock through 2030, so the flow is real. Capex-heavy players have just failed.
revenue_model: 2-4% brokerage on lot value, $1-3K per-lot assay and compliance-file fee, toll-margin on structured deals, and a monthly subscription for allocation reporting.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read Ascend and Li-Cycle as proof that battery recycling does not work. They actually proved that owning capex ahead of feedstock timing does not work. The BIS rule turned feedstock rights plus a legal wrapper into the scarce asset, and the money sits between captive sellers and stranded capacity.
first_30_days: Read the rule with a trade lawyer and publish a 6-page 'what this means for sellers' note. Cold-call scrap managers at cell plants and the top 10 aggregators. Sign 2-3 non-exclusive brokerage LOIs. Collect toll price sheets from 2 US processors and 1 Asian or European processor. Target the first structured lot in about 90 days.

title: Ritual-Accurate Wedding Data and Audits for AI
one_liner: Commission consented, styled ceremony shoots with community elders across a dozen wedding traditions, captioned by ritual stage, and sell accuracy audits and licensed datasets to image-model builders and wedding-tech companies.
customer: Generative-image model builders, stock and creative platforms with AI-licensing programs, and wedding-tech companies building AI mood boards or visualizers. Audits are $5-15k each and dataset packs are $20-150k.
problem: Image generators still get weddings wrong outside the mainstream Western template, and research on cultural bias in image models documents mis-styled Indian weddings, misidentified Korean attire and mislocalized Nigerian scenes. Web-scraped labels are worse, since 'Indian wedding' collapses Sikh, Tamil, Gujarati and Bengali ceremonies. Couples now bring AI 'inspiration' images to photographers, and wedding-tech startups embarrass themselves with visualizers that get rituals wrong in the multi-day, high-budget segments they most want. The scarce resource isn't wedding pictures, it's correctly labeled, ritual-stage-accurate images with clean releases.
solution: Rite Right runs one- and two-day ritual shoots with paid models, real officiants and community elders as advisors (no unconsented guests, so licensing is clean), photographed by working wedding pros in documentary style. Each image gets structured metadata: tradition, region, ritual stage, garment and object names, and a community-authored accuracy checklist, with model and property releases and C2PA provenance. Product one is the audit, a 'Wedding Ritual Accuracy Benchmark' (about 50 prompts per tradition) scored by elders on public and private models. Product two is licensed packs. Photographers and advisors share in license revenue.
why_now: AI-training licensing has become a real market, since Adobe and Shutterstock run contributor payout programs for training use and Getty has an OpenAI deal. Lawsuits are pushing labs toward clean, consented data, and cultural-bias evaluation of image models is an active research area. AI wedding visualizers are proliferating, and their cultural errors are viral, embarrassing and commercially costly. Audits are cheap, fast and require no dataset, so they provide first revenue while the data business builds.
revenue_model: Accuracy audits at $5-15k each (repeat quarterly as models update), dataset licensing at $20-150k per tradition pack, and rev-share to photographers and advisors. Later: a 'ritual accuracy' API for wedding-tech products.
non_obvious_insight: The photographer who has shot 40 Sikh weddings can tell in three seconds whether a laavan sequence is wrong, and that knowledge is oral, undocumented and invisible to crowd-worker labeling. What data buyers lack is not volume but the moment-by-moment ritual sequence, and only people who stand in the room at these events can supply it credibly.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 community advisors across 3 traditions from your own network. Run one styled one-day shoot on a $4-6k budget and build a 300-image sample pack with structured captions. Build a 50-prompt accuracy benchmark, score the major public image models, and publish the results as a short report to generate inbound. Email trust and safety, data and product leads at mid-size model builders and wedding-tech companies with the report and a free 10-image sample, aiming for two paid pilot audits by day 90.

title: Neutral Legacy Animal-Data Vault for NAM Validation
one_liner: A neutral data trust that turns pharma's shelved animal-study results into blinded concordance benchmarks organoid and organ-chip makers use to prove their methods are 'adequately validated.'
customer: Organoid, organ-chip and other NAM startups needing FDA-credible validation, CROs, and pharma tox groups that contribute data and earn credits.
problem: FDA's Sept 21, 2026 direct final rule swapped 'animal tests' for 'nonclinical tests' but requires methods to be 'adequately validated'. Its NAM use-case database has only 25 entries. Validation needs ground truth: in vivo and clinical outcomes for many compounds. That lives in competing pharma archives and old PDFs, and pharma cannot pool proprietary data across competitors.
solution: Contributors deposit outcomes for shelved or dead compounds (species, dose, target-organ findings, human outcome where known) into a trust with blinded, query-only access. NAM developers submit predictions on a blinded panel of 100-200 compounds. They receive sensitivity, specificity and PPV by context of use, in a format built for FDA meetings. Contributors earn free validation credits. Start from public sources: FDA and EMA review documents, NTP, open toxicogenomics sets and DILI ranking lists.
why_now: The FDA rule landed this week and the NAM database is thin. NIH turbulence pushes toward cheaper methods. The IMI eTOX project pooled 8,196 studies on 1,947 compounds from 13 pharma companies, which proves the sharing model can work, but it was a research consortium and not a validation product.
revenue_model: $20-100k per validation report, annual memberships ($50-150k for NAM vendors; $100k or in-kind data for pharma), and licensing of benchmark panels to CROs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats animal data as obsolete. As new animal studies decline, the historical archive becomes a fixed, non-renewable supply and the only ground truth for validating replacements. Dead compounds carry no competitive risk, so the usual objection to sharing disappears. The owner of the concordance yardstick becomes a toll-taker on every NAM filing.
first_30_days: Assemble a public 150-compound reference set with animal and human outcomes. Sell 3-5 'pre-validation concordance reports' at $10-20k to organ-chip and organoid startups. Interview 5 pharma tox heads about pilot contributions of 20-50 shelved compounds each. Recruit a former FDA nonclinical reviewer as an advisor.

title: Night Ledger: Sleep Evidence for Live-In Aides
one_liner: A camera-free $35 bedroom-door sensor kit that logs every night-time awakening of a dementia patient, giving live-in agencies court-grade proof of sleep or interruption, and a case for the second aide.
customer: Licensed home care agencies with 20-300 24-hour live-in cases, starting with Medicaid-contracted agencies in NYC, Long Island, Westchester and northern NJ. Secondary: families who employ live-in aides directly. Agencies pay.
problem: Live-in aides are paid for 13 of 24 hours. That is legal in New York only if the aide gets 8 hours of sleep, 5 of them uninterrupted, plus 3 hours for meals. A dementia patient who sundowns, wanders and needs toileting at 2am makes that fiction. The only evidence of sleep is the aide's own signed timesheet. Agencies face wage class actions and NYSDOL claims. Aides are underpaid and quit. The night, the most expensive and dangerous stretch of care, is the least measured.
solution: Two or three battery-powered motion or mmWave sensors (bedroom door, hallway, bathroom, exit door) and a hub that phones home. There is no video and no audio, because aides hate being watched and families in some states cannot legally record them. Each morning it produces a one-page Night Report: the longest uninterrupted stretch, the number of get-ups, exit-seeking events, and a one-tap aide confirmation of what was actually done. Quiet nights support the 13-hour pay. Noisy nights trigger a pay correction and build a documented case for the plan to authorize split-shift (two-aide) coverage. Families get 2am exit-seeking alerts on the same hardware.
why_now: In January 2026 a New York court reopened hundreds of shelved 24-hour-aide wage claims against NYSDOL and granted class certification (Legal Aid and NCLEJ). Federal DOL has only proposed reinstating the companionship exemption (July 2025). The 2013 rule is still the law, private rights of action are untouched, and state law in NY, NJ and CA applies regardless. Sensors, BLE and mmWave chips are now cheap enough to rent per case. The oldest boomers turn 80 this year, so live-in dementia cases are growing.
revenue_model: $79 per active live-in case per month, with the sensor kit rented and shipped. A one-time $1,500 to $3,000 wage-liability audit for agencies is the entry product. Families add-on at $29 per month for night alerts. Later, a fee for documentation packages that support split-shift authorization requests.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats the 13-hour rule as a labor-cost fight. Insiders know the same nightly record is a liability shield for the agency, proof of a heavier case that can justify two aides billed at full rate, and evidence for the aide, all at once. Nobody has built it because the buyer, the agency, has spent years preferring not to have the data. A class action changes that preference. Cameras are the wrong tool. Aides quit over them, and door-and-hallway motion data is enough.
first_30_days: Buy 40 off-the-shelf Zigbee or BLE motion sensors and a Pi or cellular hub. Write a script that emails a Night Report. Sell the audit as a service to 3 small LHCSAs in Brooklyn, Queens or Bergen County through wage-and-hour defense attorneys and home care association meetings, by offering a free 2-week pilot on their five heaviest cases. Ask two worker centers to beta test with aides and give aides their own copy of the log. The first paid pilots should come from agencies that were just sued or received a DOL inquiry.

title: Quality-of-Earnings Audits for Robot Fleets
one_liner: A finance-native auditor that verifies deployed units, productive hours, teleoperation share and revenue per robot for the lenders, lessors and investors underwriting robot, AV and drone fleets.
customer: Lenders, equipment lessors, SPAC sponsors, growth funds and acquirers underwriting robotics, AV and drone companies. Second wave: insurers of AV trucks and warehouse robots, and investors in robot-as-a-service lease pools.
problem: Robotics valuations run on self-reported fleet metrics. Agility reported $1.8M of 2025 revenue against a $2.5B SPAC. Maven raised $100M with about 8 robots deployed. Serve booked about $1.3k of revenue per robot. Figure reports about 740 robots against about 600 employees. 1X NEO's early demos were largely teleoperated. Nobody audits 'deployed' vs 'productive' vs 'autonomous' vs 'paid'. AV insurers price 'slightly above' human trucks on the unknown, and lessors cannot underwrite $499-$600/mo robot leases blind.
solution: A boutique assurance firm. Under NDA it gets read-only telemetry, remote-assist logs and billing, and visits sites. It produces a signed Fleet QoE report with standard metrics: units deployed vs productive hours, human interventions per robot-hour, revenue and margin per unit, safety events, uptime and maintenance cost, and contract quality. Later, publish a standard 'Fleet Passport' for covenant reporting.
why_now: About 22,000 humanoids shipped in H1 2026. Unitree IPO'd in Aug 2026. Agility is going public via SPAC. Figure plans a $600/mo lease. Skild ($14B) and Physical Intelligence ($11B) are priced for perfection. Leasing and asset-backed structures for robots are being invented now, and capital allocators need evidence, not demos.
revenue_model: $40k-$120k per diligence engagement, buyer-paid. $10k-$30k per year of continuous covenant monitoring for lenders and lessors. An anonymized benchmark data license to insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The metric that decides whether a robotics company is a software business or a labor-arbitrage business, hidden human-intervention hours per robot-hour, is invisible to the buyer. Capital allocators, not vendors, must be the payer, because vendor-paid attestation fails (Trustpilot was fined for selling to those it rates). An ex-assurance plus ex-robotics team beats a technical certifier.
first_30_days: Write a 40-item data request and an intervention-hour analysis template. Recruit an ex-Big-4 assurance lead and one robotics ops engineer. Offer two free pilot audits to a debt fund or equipment lessor with a robot deal in progress. Publish an anonymized 'what to ask a robotics CEO' metrics guide. Aim for one paid engagement letter within 60-90 days.

title: Ghost-Student Fraud Defense for Community Colleges
one_liner: Enrollment-fraud screening built into admissions and financial-aid workflows that separates real applicants from bot-driven ghost students before aid disburses.
customer: Community-college districts' admissions, financial-aid and IT-security offices, plus state college systems. There are about 1,000 community colleges in the US.
problem: Fraud rings use stolen or synthetic identities, and increasingly AI-completed coursework, to enroll and collect federal and state aid. California community colleges have reported large shares of applications as fraudulent and tens of millions of dollars lost. Regulators have tightened identity-verification requirements for aid recipients. Staff are overwhelmed by manual reviews, and consumer IDV tools do not fit education workflows.
solution: Integrate with student information and learning management systems. Risk-score at application, enrollment and first-week activity using LMS login patterns, IP and ASN reuse, device farms, writing similarity and disbursement-account reuse. Send only high-risk cases to paid ID verification, place aid holds, produce OIG-ready reports, and give auditors a dashboard.
why_now: The 2025-26 ghost-student wave hit colleges as AI agents got good enough to attend and submit work, and aid-verification rules tightened. State funding for fraud response exists.
revenue_model: $25-100K per district per year, or $0.10-0.50 per application screened.
non_obvious_insight: The budget owner is financial-aid compliance, driven by audit findings and risk to aid eligibility, not IT. The best signals (LMS behavior) exist only after enrollment, so this is behavioral IDV that consumer vendors cannot copy.
first_30_days: Pilot with 2 colleges. Retro-score one semester of application logs to show dollars at risk, pitch through financial-aid and CIO associations, and price at $2K per month.

title: Port-Level IP Shield for Indie Brands
one_liner: A subscription that registers small brands' trademarks and copyrights with CBP, feeds officers product-identification guides, and turns port detentions into evidence and settlements against the importers.
customer: Indie consumer brands with $1-30M in revenue that get cloned: fashion, toys, beauty, pet, home goods and Shopify DTC brands. They pay a monthly subscription, plus a share of any enforcement settlements.
problem: Small brands fight knockoffs with Amazon Brand Registry and platform takedowns. Those work after the goods have landed and the listings are live. Most never use the cheapest lever, which is CBP itself. Recording a mark or copyright with CBP e-Recordation costs about $190 per class. CBP can then detain suspected counterfeit or lookalike shipments at the port, and the rights-holder can get photos, samples and importer details that support demand letters and lawsuits. In practice, small brands rarely record. When CBP does ask for authentication, the brand replies late, so the goods are released.
solution: 'Port Shield' handles recordation, builds a product-identification guide (photos, tells, label details, authorized-factory MID list) that officers can use, and monitors for CBP detention and seizure notices. It answers authentication requests within CBP's short response windows, and sets up lever-rule protection against gray-market goods where it applies. It also runs a port exposure scan: lookalike listings on marketplaces matched against public bill-of-lading data to find who is shipping them into LA/Long Beach. When CBP detains a shipment, it packages the importer identity and evidence for partner IP counsel to send demand letters, and takes a share of settlements.
why_now: Generative AI has made cloning product photos and standing up dupe storefronts nearly free, so knockoff volume against small brands is rising. The 2025 de minimis clampdown, and the statutory repeal scheduled for July 2027, push formerly parcel-shipped knockoffs into entries CBP can actually target and hold. Tariff-era entries also carry much richer line-level data, which improves targeting. Long Beach hit a record August of 919,992 TEUs, so port volume is not shrinking.
revenue_model: $750 setup, then $299-$799 a month by number of marks and product lines. Enforcement adds a 20-30% share of settlements, and IP counsel pays referral fees. A later tier sells port-level counterfeit intelligence to marketplaces and insurers.
non_obvious_insight: CBP can only hold what the rights-holder helps it verify. Officers see thousands of lookalikes and act on brands that have recorded marks, supplied identification guides and answered inquiries fast. Big brands have law firms doing this. Sub-$30M brands do not know the port is a free enforcement layer, and most of the relevant customs rules are written for lawyers, not founders.
first_30_days: Pick two crowded niches, such as LA-based apparel and accessories and Shopify beauty or pet. Run free port exposure scans on 30 brands by matching lookalikes to importers in public BOL data. Cold-email the brand owners with the scan attached. Sign 5-10 brands on a paid pilot, record their marks, and produce the first product-identification guides. Line up one IP law firm as the enforcement referral partner.

title: Turn Foreman Paper Sign-In Sheets Into Court-Ready Records
one_liner: Foremen text a photo of the daily paper sign-in sheet, and the system timestamps it, flags overtime, break and travel-time errors, and builds an audit-ready record. The crew changes nothing.
customer: Trade subcontractors with 5 to 50 field employees (electrical, framing, concrete, HVAC, roofing) that still use paper sheets or Excel. It is sold through construction-focused insurance agents, payroll providers and construction CPAs.
problem: Most contractor wage-hour violations are recordkeeping failures: overtime miscalculations, uncompensated travel time and undocumented breaks. Paper sheets and foreman memory have no audit trail, so when a wage claim lands up to two years later the employer cannot prove what it paid. A $50,000 overtime dispute can double with liquidated damages before attorney fees. Owners don't buy time-tracking software for compliance, because compliance is not what they think they are buying.
solution: A phone number or WhatsApp thread. The foreman photographs the day's sign-in sheet, and the service extracts hours per worker, adds a trusted timestamp, and stores the original image in an append-only log with a chain-of-custody hash. Each week it reconciles hours against the payroll export (CSV from ADP, Gusto or QuickBooks Payroll) and flags mismatches: overtime not paid, drive time between sites, missing breaks, and prevailing-wage or certified-payroll classification gaps. When a claim or audit arrives, one click produces a records package with an affidavit-ready custodian statement. Insurance partners can offer it as a loss-control benefit on wage-and-hour or EPLI coverage.
why_now: Construction Dive ran this as a July 2026 compliance story. DOL Wage and Hour recovered more than $259 million in back wages for nearly 177,000 workers in fiscal 2025, and construction alone saw about 3,000 investigations and $36 million recovered for 21,000 workers. The labor squeeze, with job openings rising for a third month, keeps overtime and crew-hopping high. Photo capture, OCR and trusted timestamping are now cheap enough to deliver this for about $100 a month.
revenue_model: $99 to $299 per month per contractor by headcount; a $750 audit-response records package; a 15 to 20% recurring rebate to insurance agents or payroll partners who resell. Later add payroll-error recovery reports as a paid add-on.
non_obvious_insight: Apps like time clocks fail because crews resist changing habits, and buyers don't feel compliance risk. So sell defensibility on top of the existing paper behavior instead of replacing it. Evidence: a survey of 180 mid-market contractors found only 4% cited compliance as a concern with time tracking, and 72% who tracked time on paper or spreadsheets 'never raised a compliance concern once in the conversation'. The article notes the records 'can't answer the question' when disputes arise two years later, and cites $259M in DOL back wages and $36M recovered from construction in a single year (https://www.constructiondive.com/news/inaccurate-time-records-contractor-compliance-liability/825438/). The same Construction Dive labor page shows the squeeze (https://www.constructiondive.com/topic/labor/).
first_30_days: Week 1: recruit 5 contractors via a construction CPA or insurance agent friend, and build the intake as a shared phone number plus a spreadsheet and an OCR script. Weeks 2 to 3: run their real sign-in sheets through it, deliver a weekly variance report, and show each owner one specific overtime or drive-time gap. Week 4: charge $149 per month, and present the results to two construction insurance agencies as a loss-control add-on. Target: 8 paying contractors and 1 signed agency partner.

title: SOC 2 for Rent-Pricing Algorithms
one_liner: An independent audit and continuous-monitoring attestation proving an operator's revenue-management tool uses lawful inputs and real human decisions.
customer: Multifamily operators (5,000-100,000 units) using RealPage, Yardi or Entrata-style pricing in ban or enforcement jurisdictions, defendants under consent decrees needing monitors, and their insurers and lenders.
problem: Pricing tools are now legal liabilities: New York State (Dec 2025) and Berkeley ban them, San Diego levies $1,000 per violation and a UDR class action was filed, private settlements exceed $500M, and Pinnacle signed a decree Sept 4 with Camden the lone unsettled original defendant. Vendors named in suits cannot credibly certify themselves, and operators cannot prove where prices come from.
solution: Audit data lineage (any nonpublic competitor inputs, data age), analyze auto-accept and override rates and human-decision documentation, map jurisdictional exposure, and issue a signed attestation with quarterly evidence reports. License the tooling to monitors of consent decrees.
why_now: Decrees can require compliance officers and monitors, city bans are multiplying, and insurers and lenders are beginning to ask for proof.
revenue_model: $20-60K annual attestation per operator, monitor tool licenses, and insurer or broker referral arrangements.
non_obvious_insight: Independence is the product, and vendors in litigation cannot sell it. As with SOC 2 in cloud, the standard will belong to whoever writes v1 and gets insurers and lenders to accept it. Acceptance rates are the observable that plaintiffs and monitors will use.
first_30_days: Draft a 'Rent Pricing Compliance Standard v0.1' with antitrust counsel. Offer a free exposure scan to 30 operators and sign three paid design partners at a $10K discount. Approach two monitor firms and a D&O broker.

title: Recovery Audits for Downstream Tariff Refunds
one_liner: A contingency-fee recovery-audit firm that mines buyers' AP invoice history for IEEPA-era price step-ups and files contract claims against suppliers who pocketed the tariff refund.
customer: Mid-market companies that paid tariff-inflated prices but were not importer of record: hospital systems and GPOs, restaurant groups, distributors, contractors, regional retailers. They pay 20-30% of dollars recovered. Secondary buyers: importers who want a defensible refund-sharing allocation, and plaintiffs' firms that need per-customer surcharge damages.
problem: Importers stand to receive roughly $166B of IEEPA refunds. Downstream buyers who paid blended, un-itemized price increases have no easy way to size or claim their share. A commercial litigator quoted by CFO.com says his team reads hundreds of thousands of invoices by hand to compare pre-tariff and tariff-period pricing, and that many suppliers keep the refund unless asked. In parallel, at least 25 customer suits (Amazon, Costco, Walmart, Sony and others) plead unjust enrichment. Plaintiffs will need per-customer surcharge data that nobody has assembled.
solution: Ingest a buyer's AP/ERP invoice line-item export (or PDFs via extraction). Normalize SKUs and suppliers. Detect step-changes in unit price against control SKUs and commodity indices around the tariff effective dates. Infer country of origin and HTS duty exposure from public tariff tables. Estimate the IEEPA-attributable overcharge per supplier. Then generate claim packets keyed to each contract's price-adjustment, cost-pass-through or MFN clauses, with demand-letter templates and a supplier-response tracker. Start with contracts that have explicit surcharge or cost-plus language, where recovery is strongest. Partner with one or two commercial litigation boutiques for enforcement, and have human analysts review the top claims. Second product: a refund-allocation ledger for importers and distributors that want to share refunds with customers, as Williams-Sonoma and O'Reilly are doing. Third product: a damages engine for class counsel.
why_now: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026. CBP's CAPE refund portal opened April 20, 2026. CBP had paid $100B by August 7, and CAPE Phase 3 for finally liquidated entries starts October 6, 2026. An Atlanta Fed survey (September 24) says most companies will hold refunds as cash. A trade court also ruled the 10% global tariff illegal on May 7, so more refund waves may follow. Contract-notice and limitation windows are running now.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered dollars. Flat $15-50k fee for importer-side allocation reports. Per-matter fees from plaintiffs' firms. Possible later add-on: an expected-value model for funds that buy refund claims.
non_obvious_insight: For downstream buyers the refund is not a customs-law problem. It is an AP-data forensics problem, the same shape as classic recovery audits (freight, telecom, sales tax), which are paid on contingency, and the recovery-audit firms have not pivoted to it. The evidence shows the gap is manual labor: CFO.com describes lawyers examining 'hundreds of thousands of invoices' to find blended tariff pricing (https://www.cfo.com/news/these-businesses-didnt-pay-tariffs-theyre-seeking-refunds-anyway-Glen-Frost-Tim-Meyer/823107/). At least 25 customer suits need per-customer surcharge data (https://www.cfodive.com/news/amazon-companies-fighting-centralized-tariff-refund-suits-costco-cfo/830814/). Refund claims are also being sold at steep discounts (American Eagle sold $68.9M of claims for $18.6M), which shows the claims are being priced without data (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/retailers-eager-for-cash-sell-off-rights-to-potential-tariff-refunds/827064/). CBP paid $100B by August 7 (https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/cbp-has-paid-100b-in-ieepa-tariff-refunds/827257/). Main risk: B2B pass-through litigation is largely untested, so lead with contract-backed claims.
first_30_days: Pick 3 verticals with blended pricing and heavy AP volume (medical/dental supply buyers, restaurant groups, HVAC/plumbing contractors, regional grocers). Offer a free 'tariff exposure scan' from 12 months of AP export and run it on 3-5 pilot datasets. Sign a contingency engagement with a trade or commercial litigation boutique for enforcement. Build supplier claim-packet templates for the 10 most common contract clause types. Aim for the first demand letters in week 4 and first recovered dollars inside 90 days.

title: Lifetime Income Leases for Retiring Farmers' Water
one_liner: A 'water pension' that turns a retiring farm couple's senior Colorado River water right into guaranteed, inheritable lifetime income via a long-term forbearance lease, satellite-verified and sold as verified acre-feet to cities and corporates.
customer: Buyers are municipal water agencies, Lower Basin cities, corporate water-stewardship funds (such as the Water Resilience Coalition Amazon put $20M into) and conservation programs. Sellers are farm owners 62+ without farming heirs. Money moves as multi-year lease payments, and the firm keeps 8-12%.
problem: About 70% of the Colorado River goes to agriculture, and the 2027-2036 framework (Record of Decision, Aug 2026) forces the next cuts onto farms, with Powell and Mead near 36% full. 'Buy-and-dry' sales are politically toxic. Lump-sum sales trigger capital gains and do not fund a long retirement, and urban heirs inherit water rights they cannot operate. Buyers want verified acre-feet, but no settlement layer exists.
solution: A 15-30-year forbearance (rotational fallowing or deficit irrigation) on a slice of the right. Payments are indexed and pass to the surviving spouse, then to a trust. An estate-plan wrapper (trust holds the right with the lease attached, plus CPA and water-attorney advice on tax basis and long-term-care planning) makes it a retirement product. Consumptive-use reduction is verified by satellite evapotranspiration data and paid quarterly. Title never leaves the family, which defuses buy-and-dry politics for the buyer.
why_now: The 10-year framework was finalized in Aug 2026 and storage is the lowest since 1963. Corporate money is arriving ($32M raised toward a $100M goal) with no settlement layer. US drought coverage is 49.6%. A generation of irrigators is reaching retirement with no successors.
revenue_model: 8-12% of lease flows, a buyer-paid verification subscription per acre-foot, and a $3-5k planning fee per family.
non_obvious_insight: Older water-right owners often refuse to sell at any price but will accept certainty of income for life while keeping title. Water brokers are paid on transfers, not on retirements, so nobody sells water as a pension asset. The retirement-income framing is what makes the supply available.
first_30_days: Pick one district (Palo Verde Valley CA, Yuma AZ or Grand Valley CO). Run three kitchen-table workshops with an ag lender, a CPA and a water attorney to enroll about 10 couples. Get a non-binding letter of intent from one buyer for 500-2,000 acre-feet. Check the state rules on temporary transfers first.

title: Meeting Subtext Captions for Neurodivergent Workers
one_liner: An on-screen coach for Zoom and Teams that flags conversational subtext (a question aimed at you, a topic shift, rising frustration) and supports post-meeting debriefs, sold through autism and ADHD coaches.
customer: Autism and ADHD coaching practices ($40-60 per client per month), employer neurodiversity hiring programs, and state vocational rehabilitation agencies.
problem: Autistic and ADHD adults often lose jobs and friendships over unspoken social subtext rather than skill. Human job coaches cost $75-150 an hour and cannot sit in every meeting. Loneliness among autistic adults is severe, and existing tools are scripts and courses that do not work in the live moment.
solution: A client-side app reading a live transcript and showing three private cue types ('direct question to you', 'time to wrap up', 'tone: irritated'), plus post-meeting debriefs shared with the coach and a rehearsal mode simulating hard meetings. Data stays local by default, and the coach dashboard shows patterns, not raw transcripts.
why_now: Real-time multimodal models now handle affect and conversational structure at low latency. Hybrid work makes meeting transcripts routine. Employers' neurodiversity hiring programs are maturing and need retention tools.
revenue_model: Per-seat license through coaching practices, employer accommodation budgets, and state vocational rehabilitation contracts.
non_obvious_insight: The right entry point is the coach's toolkit, not the consumer app. Coaches already have the trust, the payer relationship and the clinical framing, and AI extends their reach into moments they cannot attend.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 neurodiversity coaches through ADHD and autism coach networks. Pilot with 30 clients at $50 each, collect cue accuracy ratings and coach feedback, then approach two employers' neurodiversity leads.

title: Financial-Aid Overflow Desk for New Loan Caps
one_liner: A managed service plus software that classifies programs as professional versus graduate, tracks lifetime caps and prevents mis-awards at small colleges' aid offices.
customer: Financial-aid directors and CFOs at small and mid-size, graduate-heavy private colleges and health-sciences schools.
problem: The July 1, 2026 regime capped grad loans at $20.5k a year and $100k total, gave only 11 'professional' programs $50k and $200k, and capped and prorated Parent PLUS by credit load. Final guidance came in May, vendors were not ready in August, and some disbursements ran 6 weeks late with no recourse. Errors create audit findings and student harm.
solution: An aid-regime desk: a program-classification dossier per program, cap tracking across borrowers including transfers, a Parent PLUS proration calculator, packaging letters, and a student-facing 'what you can borrow and alternatives' guide (private loan comparison, employer sponsorship, payment plan). Add a late-disbursement bridge program and audit-ready records.
why_now: This is the first aid cycle under the new rules. A pending healthcare-association lawsuit (December 2026 suspension deadline) means rules could change again, and vendors lag.
revenue_model: $25-90k per institution per year depending on graduate enrollment, plus bridge-loan fees per student.
non_obvious_insight: Every rule change is a compliance tax that lands hardest on small offices. The vendor lag is a 12-18 month window in which a service desk becomes embedded in the workflow and later converts to software.
first_30_days: Contact 20 small graduate-heavy colleges (nursing, counseling). Offer a $5k cap-readiness audit reviewing 100 student files. Publish a plain-English cap guide to generate leads and sign 3.

title: Marginalia: Lived-Experience Annotated Books
one_liner: One-of-one physical books annotated in ink by people who have actually lived what the book is about, such as a retired ER nurse in The Plague or a lighthouse keeper's daughter in To the Lighthouse.
customer: Gift buyers and collectors paying $250-1,200 per copy, quarterly-subscription readers ($180/quarter), independent bookstores, libraries and special collections, and professional associations gifting to retirees.
problem: Explanations and summaries are free and infinite, so 'I've read it' signals nothing. Celebrity-signed copies signal fame, not thought. What is scarce is a particular lived mind reading a text in real time: dated, physical, opinionated, and accountable.
solution: Recruit about 100 'readers of record': retired judges, surgeons, sommeliers, deep-sea divers, and translators. Match each to a canonical book that fits their life. Each annotates a physical copy under a fixed protocol: at least 60 marginal notes, a two-page flyleaf letter, a signed colophon, and a one-take authenticity video. Copies are numbered and sold. A commission tier lets you order a book annotated by someone in your recipient's own profession (a retirement gift for a fire chief). Displaced translators can annotate a translation against the original, showing what the machine misses.
why_now: AI summarizers have made shallow reading free, so deep, lived reading is the differentiator. The 2026 human-made premium is well documented. Physical-book culture is holding up, and the 'association copy' idea is old and understood among collectors.
revenue_model: Per-copy sales (reader 40%, platform about 45%, materials about 15%), a quarterly subscription, institutional acquisitions, and annual charity auctions of 'famous minds' copies.
non_obvious_insight: In an age of infinite explanation, the scarce good is witnessed subjectivity. A marginal note is a physical, un-averaged opinion, the opposite of what a language model produces. Collectors already pay premiums for association copies (a book owned or annotated by someone notable). This manufactures them prospectively and at scale.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 readers through retirement communities and professional associations. Produce 30 copies. Sell through a Substack with page photos and pre-orders. Approach 5 indie bookstores for consignment. Goal: $10k in pre-orders by day 60.

title: Triage Software for Satellite-SOS Rescue Teams
one_liner: Intake, deduplication and dispatch software for county and volunteer search-and-rescue teams flooded by satellite SOS messages.
customer: County sheriff SAR coordinators, state SAR coordinators, national park services and mountain rescue organizations.
problem: As satellite texting reaches ordinary phones, more people go remote and press SOS. Rescuers receive short, delayed, asynchronous messages with weak location data and many false alarms. Coordination centers were built for 911 voice calls, and volunteer teams run on spreadsheets and group texts.
solution: A gateway that ingests SOS relays (email, API, text) from phone makers and satellite messaging providers, deduplicates, geolocates, and adds terrain and weather context. It runs structured 160-character question flows, recommends the resource type to dispatch, and keeps a log for after-action review and cost recovery.
why_now: Satellite messaging on unmodified phones went mainstream across 2025-26 (the briefing shows new carrier launches as late as Sept 28, 2026). AST and SpaceX D2C are scaling, and phone makers are adding satellite SOS. The receiving end has not been rebuilt.
revenue_model: $3-15k per year per county or team. State-level contracts of $50-200k. Optional paid membership or SAR-insurance partnership.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck moved from sending distress to receiving and triaging it. Whoever owns the receive-side workflow becomes the system of record, and public agencies pay for it out of existing rescue budgets.
first_30_days: Shadow three volunteer SAR teams and one state coordinator. Build a minimal intake and dedupe tool that runs alongside their current tools. Offer it free for one summer season in exchange for a paid annual contract.

title: Package Travel Surcharge Compliance for Tour Operators
one_liner: A rules engine that calculates lawful fuel-driven price increases on already-sold package tours, generates the notices and tracks the 8% cancellation trigger.
customer: Small and mid-size EU and UK package organisers, coach-tour and cruise-package sellers, and agents acting as organisers with EUR 5-200M in sales, plus their bonding insurers.
problem: With the Hormuz closure and soaring jet fuel, packages sold months ago are underwater and airlines are cutting capacity and raising fares. Under EU and UK package rules an organiser can raise prices only if the contract allows it, only for fuel, tax or exchange-rate changes, with at least 20 days' notice, and an increase above 8% lets travellers cancel free. Organisers must also pass on decreases. Spreadsheet errors mean refunds and regulator complaints.
solution: Connect to booking exports, model the cost components per trip, compute the lawful pass-through per contract clause, and generate localised notices with timelines. Track the 8% threshold and deadlines, keep an audit trail for regulators and bonding insurers, and flag contracts whose clauses need rewriting.
why_now: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed on 2 Mar 2026 and, by September, budget carriers cite soaring fuel costs with capacity cuts and fare hikes ahead. Shorter booking lead times (33 days versus 37.5) do not help packages sold long in advance.
revenue_model: EUR 300-1,500 per month per operator or about 0.1% of sales, plus per-notice fees and clause redesign consulting.
non_obvious_insight: In a cost shock much of the loss is legal rather than commercial. Operators eat costs because they misread pass-through limits or send defective notices, so compliance software turns panic into recovered margin.
first_30_days: Build a calculator and notice templates in a spreadsheet plus an LLM. Publish a gated '2026 fuel surcharge playbook' through trade associations, and sell 10 operators at EUR 500 per month.

title: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge Eligibility and Prior-Auth Navigator
one_liner: A 2-minute eligibility check and clinician-ready prior-auth packet for the $50/month Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, sold to caregivers, independent pharmacies and primary-care offices before the window closes in December 2027.
customer: Two payers. (a) Gen X adult children (45-58, household income often above $100K) who manage a Medicare-age parent's medications and pay $29 per packet. (b) Independent pharmacies and small primary-care practices that pay $79/month to stop fielding the same eligibility and prior-auth questions by phone.
problem: Medicare started an 18-month GLP-1 Bridge on July 1, 2026. It costs $50/month for Wegovy, Zepbound or Foundayo, but eligibility is a maze. It needs a BMI of 35 or more, or BMI 30+ with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, uncontrolled hypertension or stage 3a+ kidney disease, or BMI 27+ with pre-diabetes, prior heart attack or stroke, or symptomatic peripheral artery disease. Type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea and MASH disqualify you. So does having filled any GLP-1 under Part D in 2026. Prior authorization is required. Roughly 3.8M Part D enrollees qualify and about 5.9M are locked out, so sicker patients are routed to Part D copays of $200-600+ a month. One 68-year-old retired professor with BMI 42, a quadruple bypass and sleep apnea told KFF Health News: 'I'm obese, morbidly obese, BMI 42... And yet I can't get it.'
solution: A plain-language quiz built from the published Bridge criteria. It flags the traps, such as a 2026 Part D GLP-1 fill or a sleep apnea diagnosis. It outputs one of three routes: Bridge, Part D with an expected copay, or a manufacturer cash price (TrumpRx lists $149-$299/month). It then generates a prior-authorization documentation checklist and cover letter for the prescriber (BMI evidence, comorbidity codes, exclusion attestation). Pharmacies and practices get a white-label link and a shared queue of who is waiting on what. It stays plan-neutral: no plan enrollment and no commissions from carriers, which keeps it outside Medicare marketing rules (confirm with counsel).
why_now: The Bridge began July 1, 2026 and ends December 2027, so the demand window is 15 months and open enrollment starts October 15, about 3 weeks from now. CMS is also ending the Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration after 2026. That subsidy had cut average premiums by $26 in 2025 and $16 in 2026, and about 24.9M people are in stand-alone drug plans that may face bigger 2027 increases. Oral options (Wegovy pill approved December 2025, Foundayo approved April 2026) widen the eligible pool. Nobody has built a workflow product for a program this new and this temporary.
revenue_model: $29 one-time per beneficiary packet (caregiver-paid). $79/month per independent pharmacy or clinic for white-label link, queue and templates. Optional $15 per completed PA-submission assist. Sunset risk is real, so design the engine to carry over to whatever CMS replaces the Bridge with (KFF flags a coming BALANCE model).
non_obvious_insight: The eligibility rules create a paradox where the sicker you are, the more you pay. Sleep apnea or diabetes disqualifies patients from the $50 Bridge and pushes them into $200-600+ Part D copays, which can exceed manufacturer cash prices ($199 Wegovy pen, $299 Zepbound on TrumpRx). That gap creates demand for a neutral router rather than another telehealth prescriber. Evidence: KFF's Bridge criteria, cost and start/end dates https://www.kff.org/medicare/nearly-four-million-medicare-beneficiaries-met-the-eligibility-criteria-in-2023-for-the-medicare-glp-1-bridge/ ; the excluded-patient quote, 5.9M figure and Part D copay range https://kffhealthnews.org/aging/medicare-glp1-bridge-weight-loss-drugs-coverage-exceptions-cost-access/ ; premium-subsidy end and 24.9M stand-alone enrollees https://www.kff.org/quick-insights/cmss-decision-to-end-temporary-subsidies-to-medicares-stand-alone-drug-plans-could-mean-larger-premium-increases-for-some-beneficiaries-next-year/ ; cash prices https://trumprx.gov/ . To verify: whether Medicare beneficiaries can actually use cash-price channels, and how those purchases interact with Part D cap accounting. One fetched source (Wikipedia) implies TrumpRx has Medicare-specific pricing, which conflicts with the site's consumer prices.
first_30_days: Week 1: turn the KFF criteria into a quiz and publish 'Do I qualify for the $50 Medicare GLP-1 Bridge?' pages timed to the October 15 open-enrollment spike. Week 2: post in Medicare and caregiver communities and pitch 10 independent pharmacies (NCPA-style networks) on a free white-label link. Week 3: get one primary-care practice to review the PA cover-letter template for clinical accuracy. Week 4: charge $29 for the packet. Target 100 paid packets and 5 pharmacies on $79/month. Keep it free of plan recommendations until compliance is reviewed.

title: Live-In Caretaker Tenants for Homes in Probate
one_liner: A managed service that places vetted short-term tenants in homes stuck in probate. The rent covers carrying costs, the occupied status keeps the house insured, and the estate gets a caretaker instead of a vacant liability.
customer: Executors and heirs (often out-of-state and aged 50-65), and the probate attorneys, realtors and bank trust officers who advise them. Tenants (traveling nurses, displaced workers, downsizing seniors) pay a reduced rent.
problem: Probate takes months to a year and a half, and the house sits empty. Standard homeowner policies typically restrict coverage after 30-60 days of vacancy, and vacant-property policies cost far more. Break-ins and burst pipes are common, and the executor pays taxes, utilities and insurance. August 2026 was the strongest buyer's market on Redfin's record (58% more sellers than buyers, 44.7% of sales with concessions), so sales take longer. Meanwhile 20% of renter households paid late or missed rent in 2025.
solution: Provide a state-specific rolling license or lease template (executor-authority checked by counsel), tenant vetting, an occupied-dwelling insurance rider through a partner MGA, utilities in the caretaker's name, monthly inspections, an inventory with valuables and documents locked away, and a clean turnover at closing. Tenants pay about 70-85% of market rent. The estate pays a flat management fee that is typically below its avoided vacancy costs. The referral funnel is estate attorneys and probate realtors.
why_now: Rates near 7.5% and record concessions lengthen time-to-sale. The first wave of the wealth transfer is spousal, and hundreds of thousands of homes a year pass through death. Middle-income rent distress is at a series high, and rents are flat nationally, so a discounted, furnished, month-to-month home has a ready tenant pool. AI-armed pro se tenants are a rising risk, which makes well-drafted licenses and vetting a real edge.
revenue_model: About 10% of rent or a flat $250 per month per house, a setup fee, insurance and utility referral commissions, and an upsell into cleanout, staging and listing.
non_obvious_insight: The dead-owner house is the one kind of housing supply that is empty by legal necessity rather than by demand. It stays empty because nobody has authority, insurance or know-how to rent it. Probate delay is a housing-supply constraint disguised as a legal process.
first_30_days: Sign three probate attorneys as partners. Have counsel draft a license for one state. Recruit about 10 tenant candidates through traveling-nurse agencies, colleges and displaced-worker groups. Get an MGA to quote an occupied rider. Pilot three houses in one county.

title: Chaos Testing for Buildings as Code-Required Commissioning
one_liner: An agent that safely actuates a building's HVAC at night, forcing dampers, valves and pumps through scripted step tests, to produce the functional-test evidence that codes require and passive analytics cannot.
customer: Commissioning firms and energy-service companies, and owners of 100k-2M sq ft commercial buildings facing performance standards (NYC Local Law 97, Washington and Denver building performance standards) and California Title 24 acceptance testing.
problem: Passive fault-detection analytics cannot tell 'stuck damper' from 'no demand'. Functional performance tests are still done by hand on clipboards at handover and rarely repeated, so buildings drift into waste. Emissions penalties and code-required acceptance tests raise the stakes, yet commissioning agents are labor-constrained.
solution: Connect through a BACnet or BAS gateway with read/write access. An LLM converts Sequences of Operation (ASHRAE Guideline 36 or project spec PDFs) into bounded test scripts with safety envelopes and automatic rollback. Overnight runs produce pass/fail results with evidence, a deficiency list with estimated savings, and signed test reports for compliance. Re-run quarterly, with operator approval built in.
why_now: BAS gateways and cloud connections are mainstream. LLMs can now parse sequences and generate test logic. Building performance standards, including LL97, are producing real penalties, and utilities pay for measured savings. Commissioning firms cannot hire enough engineers.
revenue_model: $5-15k per building test campaign, $1-3k per month for ongoing quarterly testing, white-label resale through commissioning firms at about 30% margin, and shared-savings deals with ESCOs.
non_obvious_insight: Active probing creates ground-truth labels that passive analytics lack, and the law already requires many of the tests, so automating them cuts a mandatory cost rather than selling a discretionary energy project. Chaos engineering is routine in software but almost unknown in buildings because nobody trusts write access, so the real product is the safety envelope, rollback and operator sign-off, more than the AI.
first_30_days: Partner with two commissioning-authority firms. Agree on five common tests (economizer, VAV minimum flow, chiller staging, sensor cross-checks, pump changeover). Run them on 3 buildings with BACnet access at a fixed fee priced at 40-60% of a manual test, and document the energy findings.

title: Rails Weather: Live Nigerian Payment Reliability Index
one_liner: An independent, always-on measurement of which bank-to-bank transfers are actually working right now, sold as an API and SLA evidence.
customer: Payment service providers, aggregators and mid-size fintechs that route transfers; large merchants and marketplaces; fintech partnership desks that need evidence in disputes with sponsor banks. Consumers get a free status page.
problem: Every Nigerian fintech founder knows transfer success varies by bank pair and hour. It drops at month-end salary rushes, on Friday evenings, and during weekend core-banking upgrades. Worst of all is the 'pending' or 'successful but not credited' limbo. Nobody publishes independent data, bank status pages are unreliable, and fintechs keep private dashboards. Users cope by keeping 3-5 accounts and switching to whichever works, and merchants insist on POS because they distrust transfers. Small fintechs cannot prove to sponsor banks or regulators where the failures originate.
solution: Run automated, staggered probe transfers between the team's own accounts across the top 10-15 banks and fintechs, measuring success rate, time-to-credit and the pending-then-resolve rate. Only the transfer fee is lost, since the money returns to a team account. Publish a free public status page for reach. Sell a routing-intelligence API (best rail or account right now, expected delay), monthly SLA-evidence reports, and alerts. Later, add a privacy-safe data co-op in which fintechs contribute anonymised outcome counts in exchange for deeper, real-time bank-pair data.
why_now: CBN moved 2026 into an enforcement year, with open banking, APP-fraud and failed-transaction rules all coming due together. Fintechs now have to show measured reliability, not just assert it. POS and transfer volume has exploded (5.9 million active POS terminals; N10.5 trillion of POS transactions in Q1 2025 alone). Cheap serverless probing and LLM-written incident summaries make a two-person team viable.
revenue_model: API subscription tiers of about N250k to N3m per month depending on volume. Enterprise SLA and dispute-evidence reports at N1-5m per report. A data-co-op membership fee. A sponsored 'Nigeria Payments Index' report for banks and media.
non_obvious_insight: The key metric is time-to-credit and the size of the ambiguous-pending bucket, not success rate. Banks report 'success' at the API level while customers wait hours. Independent measurement is also the only neutral evidence in the fight between sponsor banks and fintechs over who caused a failure, and neither side can publish it themselves.
first_30_days: Open business accounts at 8-10 institutions. Write a probe scheduler that costs roughly N3m per month at a 15-minute cadence across about 100 pairs. Publish a public dashboard and a weekly 'worst bank pairs' thread that the fintech community shares. Offer 5 fintech CTOs a free 60-day API trial in return for feedback and sample failure logs. Convert the first 2-3 to paid once their own incident data lines up with the index.

title: Code-Cleared Church Space for Microschools
one_liner: Pair congregations with empty classroom wings and microschool or childcare operators, and sell the missing piece: pre-cleared zoning, fire and licensing paths.
customer: Microschool founders, learning-pod operators and small childcare providers who pay rent, and shrinking congregations, lodges and libraries with weekday space. Operators pay a platform fee; congregations pay for readiness passports.
problem: Microschool enrollment has grown an estimated 40% since 2023, and ESAs plus a federal scholarship tax credit starting in 2027 will add demand. Space is not the constraint; permission is. Certificate-of-occupancy, fire-marshal, egress, sprinkler and childcare-licensing rules vary by jurisdiction, so operators guess and congregations do not know what their building could legally host.
solution: For each listed building, produce a jurisdiction-specific readiness passport: occupancy class, likely deficiencies with cost estimates, pre-drawn plan sets, checklist and sequencing for approvals. Add a standard lease, child-protection policy pack and insurance bundle. Operators search by county and see how many weeks and dollars separate them from opening.
why_now: ESAs, tax-credit scholarships and state laws (Florida now lets registered microschools use former churches and similar buildings without zoning changes) are moving faster than building codes. Congregations are shrinking and buildings are costly to maintain. Treasury rulemaking on what counts as a school adds uncertainty that rewards jurisdiction-specific expertise.
revenue_model: $2k to $6k per building readiness passport, 5% of first-year rent or $250 to $500 a month platform fee from operators, insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Listing space is a commodity. Pre-cleared certainty is the product, and the code-path knowledge compounds jurisdiction by jurisdiction. Each solved county becomes a reusable playbook and a barrier to competitors.
first_30_days: Pick one state that has ESAs and friendly rules (Florida, Texas, Arizona or Tennessee). Map the approval path in 3 counties. Sign 5 churches and 5 microschool operators through founder groups. Deliver the first paid passport for $3k with a code consultant.
